적다.x: This restaurant has few customers today.
적다.t: A different verb 적다 means 'to write down'.

적다.x: Please write your name and phone number here.
적다.e: Homonym warning: the adjective 적다 means 'few, little'.
적다.t: Pronounced [적따]; 적다 means jotting down info, while 쓰다 covers all writing.

기차역.ex: 내일 아침에 기차역에서 친구를 만나기로 했어요.
기차역.x: I'm meeting a friend at the train station tomorrow morning.
기차역.e: 기차 is literally 'steam vehicle', from the days of steam trains.

혹시.m: by any chance, perhaps; just in case
혹시.x: Is there a pharmacy around here, by any chance?
혹시.e: Literally 'perhaps it is' — a soft opener for questions.
혹시.t: Starting a question with 혹시 makes it sound softer and more polite.

평소.ex: 오늘은 평소보다 한 시간 일찍 일어났어요.
평소.x: Today I got up an hour earlier than usual.
평소.e: Literally 'ordinary and plain', your normal everyday state.
평소.t: Mostly used as 평소에 'usually', 평소처럼 'as usual', or 평소보다 'than usual'.

박수.x: When the song ended, everyone clapped.
박수.t: Pronounced [박쑤]. Clap is 박수를 치다; hosts say 박수 부탁드립니다 'a round of applause, please'.

황사.ex: 봄에는 황사 때문에 하늘이 노랗게 보여요.
황사.x: In spring the sky looks yellow because of yellow dust.
황사.e: Literally 'yellow sand,' blown in from deserts each spring.

학과.x: I'm a junior in the business department at my university.

이기적.ex: 자기 생각만 하는 것은 너무 이기적이에요.
이기적.x: Thinking only about yourself is too selfish.
이기적.t: Used like an adjective: 이기적이다, or 이기적인 + noun (이기적인 사람 = a selfish person).

깍두기.x: Kkakdugi goes really well with seolleongtang.
깍두기.e: Native word linked to 깍둑 'in chunky cubes', as in 깍둑썰기 'dicing'.
깍두기.t: Pronounced [깍뚜기]. Casually, it also means a kid who can join either team in a game.

예방 접종.ex: 아이들은 정해진 시기에 예방 접종을 받아야 해요.
예방 접종.x: Children need to get their vaccinations at set times.
예방 접종.e: Literally 'prevent beforehand' plus 'graft a seed' — planting immunity in advance.
예방 접종.t: Say 예방 접종을 하다/받다; with 주사 it's 예방 주사를 맞다.

명문대.x: He graduated from a top university and joined a major company.
명문대.e: Literally 'famous-gate university'; short for 명문 대학.

원자력.ex: 원자력은 전기를 많이 만들지만 위험할 수도 있어요.
원자력.x: Nuclear power produces a lot of electricity, but it can be dangerous.

상실감.ex: 반려견이 죽은 후 큰 상실감을 느꼈어요.
상실감.x: After my dog died, I felt a deep sense of loss.
상실감.e: -감 = a feeling or sense: 상실감, 우울감, 자신감.

씁쓸하다.ex: 친구가 내 생일을 잊어버려서 좀 씁쓸했어요.
씁쓸하다.x: My friend forgot my birthday, so I felt a bit bitter.
씁쓸하다.e: Built from 쓰다 'bitter' — a taste word that also describes a disappointed feeling.

긁다.m: to scratch; to scrape; (slang) to swipe (a card)
긁다.ex: 모기에 물린 데를 자꾸 긁지 마세요.
긁다.x: Don't keep scratching the mosquito bite.
긁다.t: Pronounced [극따]; before a vowel both sound: 긁어요 [글거요].

열을 받다.m: to get angry, to get worked up, to be ticked off
열을 받다.ex: 친구가 약속을 또 어겨서 열을 받았어요.
열을 받다.x: My friend broke our plans again, and I got really mad.
열을 받다.e: Literally 'to receive heat,' like a kettle coming to a boil.
열을 받다.t: Casual and a bit slangy; in formal situations say 화가 나다 instead.

송전.ex: 마을 주민들이 송전탑 건설에 반대하고 있습니다.
송전.x: The villagers are opposing the construction of transmission towers.

압도하다.m: to overwhelm, to overpower, to dominate
압도하다.ex: 그 팀은 경기 내내 상대를 압도했어요.
압도하다.x: That team dominated its opponent throughout the game.
압도하다.t: The adjective form 압도적인 (overwhelming) is very common: 압도적인 승리 = a landslide victory.

꿰뚫다.m: to pierce; to see through, to have a deep grasp of
꿰뚫다.ex: 그 교수님은 업계의 흐름을 꿰뚫고 계세요.
꿰뚫다.x: That professor has a deep grasp of industry trends.
꿰뚫다.e: Built from 꿰다 'to thread' plus 뚫다 'to bore through.'
꿰뚫다.t: Pronounced [꿰뚤타]. 훤히 꿰뚫다 means 'to know inside out.'

십시일반.m: many small contributions adding up; everyone chipping in
십시일반.ex: 동료들이 십시일반 돈을 모아 그를 도왔어요.
십시일반.x: His coworkers each chipped in a little money to help him.
십시일반.e: Literally 'ten spoonfuls make one bowl of rice.'

박차를 가하다.forms: 박차를 가해요 · 박차를 가했어요 · ~에 박차를 가하다
박차를 가하다.m: to speed up; to spur on; to step up efforts
박차를 가하다.ex: 정부가 신도시 건설에 박차를 가하고 있습니다.
박차를 가하다.x: The government is speeding up construction of the new town.
박차를 가하다.e: 박차 = a rider's spur; literally 'to apply the spur.'

필연성.ex: 두 사건 사이에 필연성이 있다고 보기는 어려워요.
필연성.x: It's hard to say there's a necessary link between the two events.
필연성.t: Pronounced [피련썽]: ㄹ carries over into the next syllable.

금단 현상.ex: 담배를 끊은 후 심한 금단 현상을 겪었어요.
금단 현상.x: After quitting smoking, I went through severe withdrawal symptoms.
금단 현상.e: Literally 'phenomenon of cutting off what's forbidden'.
금단 현상.t: Used jokingly too: 스마트폰 금단 현상 means feeling lost without your phone.

기대 수명.ex: 한국인의 기대 수명은 계속 늘어나고 있습니다.

자의식.ex: 사춘기에는 자의식이 강해져서 남의 시선을 신경 써요.
자의식.x: In puberty, self-consciousness grows and teens worry about how others see them.
자의식.t: 자의식 과잉 is a common phrase for someone who thinks everyone is watching them.

조울증.x: With bipolar disorder, your mood swings to extremes.
조울증.t: Pronounced [조울쯩]; casually people may say 조울증 같아 about mood swings, but it can sound insensitive.

애틋하다.m: to be tender and affectionate (with longing); touching, poignant
애틋하다.ex: 두 사람의 애틋한 사랑 이야기가 감동적이었어요.
애틋하다.x: The two people's tender love story was moving.
애틋하다.e: Probably from 애 'heart, insides' as in 애타다: love mixed with ache.
애틋하다.t: Pronounced [애트타다]; captures affection tinged with longing, often for family or distant lovers.

식물인간.ex: 그는 사고 후 몇 년째 식물인간 상태로 지내고 있어요.
식물인간.x: He has been in a vegetative state for years since the accident.
식물인간.e: Literally 'plant person' — alive but without awareness.

청원.ex: 시민들은 국회에 법 개정을 요구하는 청원을 냈습니다.
청원.x: Citizens submitted a petition to the National Assembly calling for a change in the law.

정수.m: essence, quintessence, the very best part
정수.ex: 이 음식은 한국 전통 요리의 정수를 보여 줘요.
정수.x: This dish shows the essence of traditional Korean cooking.
정수.t: Homonyms: 정수 also means 'integer' and 'purified water.'
